name: Reveal an area
summary: On a key, the unit uncovers an area for its whole team for a short time: it scans a spot, often far away, fires or places a sensor that pulses, or deploys into a sensor post. Everything inside shows up for the team, including enemies that are normally hidden (cloaked, burrowed, stealthed, tunnelling or submerged units, and fakes) and anything behind walls or under the fog. Some versions keep tracking the enemies they caught after those move away; a few sweep the whole map for one kind of target. The reveal gives information, not damage, so it pays off only when the team acts on it. It is the ability home of the detector sensor trait: a unit that detects all the time uses the trait instead.
counterplay: Leave the scanned area before the team can act, or stand still against motion sensors, which miss enemies that are not moving.
Destroy the sensor: placed sensors and bolts are fragile and give themselves away by their pulse.
Show yourself to bait the scan out, then move in while it is on cooldown.
Stay out of the sensor's line of sight where it needs one (a recon bolt reveals only what it can see).
Hunt the scanner: a deployed sensor post cannot move, and most scanning units are lightly armed.

other_examples.note: A building's ability that can target any spot on the map: it lights up a circle there for several seconds and shows hidden units in it (cloaked, burrowed, or fake ones made by hallucination). Players scan to scout tech and to fight cloaked attackers, and each scan spends energy that would otherwise buy extra income.

sources.title: Scanner Sweep, Liquipedia StarCraft II Wiki

other_examples.note: The Oracle marks a circle; every enemy unit inside, seen or hidden, is revealed and keeps giving vision around itself for a while as it moves. Players use it to track armies, to uncover burrowed units without a detector, and to let long-range units fire at their full reach.

A support vehicle that has to deploy before its sensors work. Deployed, it finds cloaked and tunnelling enemy units and buildings around it and shows them on the radar and on screen, though they stay cloaked, so others must still attack them; it does not show on enemy radar itself.

sources.title: Mobile sensor array, Command & Conquer Wiki
sources.note: Its quote box copies the Tiberian Sun manual's entry.

other_examples.note: A cheap upgrade gives the unarmed van a scan it can aim at a small area anywhere on the map, showing it for a moment and exposing any stealthed units or buildings there. The van also detects stealth near itself all the time, which is the detector trait, not this pattern.
For a munitions cost and on a cooldown, the mortar fires a flare that drifts down on a parachute over a chosen spot and reveals the area around it for a good while.

sources.title: PM-41 82mm Mortar Squad, Company of Heroes Wiki

shooter_analogues.note: A sensor the Recon places on the ground. Every few seconds it pulses, through walls, and puts moving enemies within its radius on the team's minimap with a beep; enemies who stand still, crouch or go prone are not picked up, and a few bullets destroy it.

sources.title: T-UGS, Battlefield Wiki
sources.note: Its quote boxes copy the Battlelog gadget descriptions (Battlefield 3 and 4) and the in-game descriptions (Battlefield 2042 and 6).

shooter_analogues.note: He fires an arrow that can bounce before it sticks; it then sends out a few sonar pulses, and any enemy in its line of sight is briefly shown to his team as a silhouette. Enemies can shoot the bolt to stop it.

sources.title: Recon Bolt, Valorant Wiki
sources.note: Its Description quote box copies the in-game ability description.

shooter_analogues.note: A scan on a cooldown that sweeps a wide cone ahead, through structures, and highlights enemies, traps and clues for the whole squad for a moment, also telling how many enemies it found.

player_translation.summary: A key that lights up an area for the whole team for a few seconds: hidden, cloaked or burrowed enemies there appear on every teammate's screen and minimap. The player trades their own damage for the team's information.
as_user: Scan where trouble is coming: a flank, a capture point, the gap a cloaked enemy has to cross, or the ground your artillery wants to hit.
Placed versions keep watch for you: drop a sensor on a flank and get a ping when someone moves past it.
Call what you see: a reveal is wasted unless teammates act on it, so the pattern rewards pings and voice chat.
Long-range versions scout from safety; deployed versions turn you into a fixed sensor post that the team has to guard.
as_target: A visible pulse or sweeping ring and a sound tell you that you have been revealed; you have a few seconds before the enemy team reacts.
Leave the scanned area, or freeze against motion sensors.
Destroy placed sensors; they are fragile and their pulse gives them away.
As a cloaked or stealthy unit, break line of sight and move as soon as a scan passes over you instead of staying in the open.
teammates: Spotter: the scanner finds targets for snipers, artillery and called strikes beyond their own sight.
Stealth counter: it is the team's answer to cloak, burrow, stealth and shroud fields.
On the other side, cloaked and stealthy players must work together to waste the scan or kill the sensor.
controls: Q scans: hold Q to show the scan circle under the cursor within range (a map view for off-screen versions), release to scan.
Placed-sensor variant: Q throws or drops a sensor; with the cursor on one of your own sensors, Q picks it back up.
Deployed-array variant: Q deploys (you cannot move while deployed), Q again packs up.
feedback: A team-coloured ring sweeping outward from the scan point, visible to both teams.
Revealed enemies get an outline shown through fog and walls for the reveal's length, plus minimap dots for the team.
Revealed players see an eye or radar icon on their HUD and hear a ping.
Placed sensors pulse visibly and beep, so enemies can find and shoot them.
changes_from_rts: RTS scans are often map-wide or side-wide powers (the StarCraft II Scanner Sweep from a building, the Red Alert 1 spy's sonar pulse that shows every submarine); here the scan sits on one unit with a cooldown and a limited range.
The spy earns its pulse once, by getting into an enemy building; here it becomes a normal key on a cooldown, or a charge earned from an objective.
The revealed player must be told, so stealth players are not hunted without warning.
Information must reach teammates at once: revealed targets are pinged on the minimap automatically.
Keep the reveal short (a few seconds), so stealth units keep a role.

team_play.notes: A pure team tool: the scanner rarely gets the kill but makes it possible for snipers, artillery and anyone hunting stealth units; the enemy's stealth players must work together to dodge or kill the sensors.

notes: Needs per-team vision with fog of war, so a reveal can show an area and its units to one team only.
Every hidden state the scan uncovers (cloak, burrow, stealth, and disguise if the open question on it is answered yes) needs a revealed override with a timer.
Placed sensors need health, pulses and minimap pings.
What each team may see must be decided on the server, or players can cheat vision.
Scans that are too frequent or too wide make every stealth unit useless; keep reveals short and on a cooldown.
Map-wide reveals give away whole plans; keep the range limited.
With long-range strikes on the same team, a scan lets the team hit anything anywhere; tie strike range to the striker's own reach.
Revealed enemies need one consistent highlight that differs from plain sight.
Players must always know when they are revealed and for how long.

variants.name: Pulse scan
variants.summary: Aim a circle at range; the area and every hidden enemy inside show for a few seconds.
variants.seen_in: StarCraft II Scanner Sweep; Generals Radar Van Scan; Company of Heroes 2 mortar flare

variants.name: Cone sweep
variants.summary: A short sweep in a wide cone ahead of you, through walls, that highlights everyone it finds for a moment.
variants.seen_in: Apex Legends Bloodhound's Eye of the Allfather

variants.name: Placed sensor
variants.summary: Throw or drop a sensor that keeps pulsing and pings moving enemies near it until it is destroyed.
variants.seen_in: Battlefield T-UGS; Valorant Sova's Recon Bolt (pulses for a few seconds)

variants.name: Tracking reveal
variants.summary: Enemies caught in the scan stay revealed for a while as they move, each giving vision around itself.

variants.name: Deployed array
variants.summary: Deploy into a sensor post that keeps showing hidden enemies around you while you stay put; pack up to move.

variants.name: Global class ping
variants.summary: Briefly show every enemy of one kind (submarines, cloaked units, burrowed units) anywhere on the map.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 1 Spy's Sonar Pulse (every enemy submarine on the map)

adds_strengths.why: Finds hidden enemies and targets for the team beyond its own sight.

adds_weaknesses.why: Information only: the scan deals no damage, and a wasted one leaves the team blind until the cooldown ends.

counters.why: Stealthy units are shown to the whole team for as long as the reveal lasts.
Cloaked units inside the scan are uncovered for the team.
Burrowed or submerged units inside the scan are uncovered for the team.
A scan lights up what hides under a shroud field, at least for a moment.

countered_by.why: Fast units are out of the scanned area before the team can act on what it showed.
A head-on armoured push does not rely on hiding, so the scan has little to uncover.

open_questions: Should a scan also expose disguised players, as the detector sensor trait does, or only cloaked and burrowed ones?
Should revealed players be told they are revealed? (Recommended: yes, with an icon and a sound.)
Map-wide reveals of one unit type (the Red Alert 1 sonar pulse): allow them only at T3, or not at all?

shooter_fit.reason: Recon scans and sensors are standard in team shooters (Battlefield, Valorant, Apex) and suit a top-down camera, where shared vision and the minimap carry most of the information.

review.notes: Re-checked field by field against its sources by the batch r1 checker, which covered all 33 batch patterns; research/r1/checker/checks.json lists every field and verdict. The wrong paths were fixed as the skeptic confirmed (cbe6de8).
